newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican Cetes rates rise on inflation concerns.
newsitem.headline: Mexican Cetes rates rise on inflation concerns.

text.p: Mexico's primary Cetes rates rose in the shorter terms but fell slightly in the one-year term at Tuesday's auction, reflecting increasing near-term inflationary pressures, analysts said.
"The short-term paper responded mainly to expected higher inflation in coming months," said Ricardo Vazquez, an analyst with Banco Union.

At Tuesday's Banco de Mexico auction, the one-month Cetes rate rose 44 basis points to 29.89 percent, the 91-day paper rate rose 78 basis points to 29.68 percent, and the rate on the 182-day Cetes rose 38 basis points to 28.07 percent.
Last week, 364-day paper yielded 27.15 percent, while this week 357-day paper yielded 27.12 percent.
Analysts have said that room for short-term interest rates to drop has been reduced due to an expected rise in inflationary pressures before the end of the year.

"We believe seasonal factors, peso depreciation, and scheduled wage/price increases in December will force prices to rise at a rate of around two percent over the next two months bringing the 1996 year-end CPI inflation rate to nearly 27 percent," Credit Suisse said in a recent report.
The meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee on November 13 has also added an element of uncertainty to markets in Mexico, although the Fed is seen leaving rates unchanged.

Another factor weighing on interest rates has been the results of elections held in the states of Mexico, Coahuila and Hidalgo on Sunday, where the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) suffered dramatic setbacks.
But perspectives of a decline in inflation over the medium-term have helped longer-term Cetes rates to fall and keep the yield curve inverted.

"The yield curve is expected to remain inverted through to the end of this year, with the short-end pressured higher by year-end factors, pacto-related price and wage increases biasing the December (and possibly January) inflation rates higher," said MMS International.
The pacto is a government, business and labour alliance that sets certain wage and price increases.
The bellwether one-month rate fell to 22.74 percent on October 8 but rose sharply during a period of peso instability in late October.
The exchange rate has remained calm recently, and that has helped interest rates to stabilise as well.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed 1.1 centavos weaker at 7.9050/7.9100 per dollar on Tuesday.
